stories.title: U.S. withdrawal from Iraq is complete
stories.summary: Twenty-three years after President George W. Bush's campaign of "shock and awe," the U.S. military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.

stories.title: France arrests 5,000 people, mostly teens, as school protests spread
stories.summary: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.

stories.title: 'It's not just a Cornell problem': Students speak out about sexual assault
stories.summary: Women are posting videos hashtagged #IAmJaneDoe to support the woman suing Cornell. Students across the country say her case raises concerns about safety on campus.

stories.title: Lula or Bolsonaro? Some Brazilian voters say they don't want either
stories.summary: Brazil's election enters its final day of campaigning as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their last pitches to voters. Brazilians explain what worries them, and why some still can't choose.

stories.title: From saunas to psychedelics, how a health reporter sorts science from hype
stories.summary: A reporting trip to a sauna conference in Oslo found NPR's Will Stone in a sauna with his clothes and recording gear. In this reporter's notebook, he explains how he investigates the science behind wellness claims.

stories.title: The Tonics: suburban a cappella singers are improbable social media stars
stories.summary: After three decades, an aging male acapella group is building a following by posting video of their rehearsals around suburban, island kitchens. How the Tonics turned social media shade into success.
